description: Hibernates a server: once hibernated it is billed a much lower HIBERNATION RATE (shown by gpucloud_get_server under hibernation, and returned by this tool as hibernationFee) instead of its hourly rate, for as long as it exists: tell the user this cost before hibernating; to stop paying entirely, delete the server. The system disk is kept; the WORK DISK (high-capacity local storage) is ERASED, and memory and running processes are lost: tell the user to copy important data elsewhere first (the answer carries notKept). With the backup option on, the system disk is backed up first (about 12 more minutes, billed normally; the answer carries backupFirst), then the server is hibernated automatically. The public IP address is RELEASED: a new, different one is assigned on restore, and SSH may then report a changed host key for it. Restore it later with gpucloud_restore_server: restoring takes a few minutes and depends on GPU availability. An hourly server you hibernate is kept as long as the account has credit left; once the credit is exhausted, it is deleted with its data after three notices, never within 72 h of the hibernation (tell the user). The answer carries customerHibernation (maxHours, message; deleteAt is always null: no date while credit remains). (permission: servers:hibernate) [Requires a free GPU Cloud account and MCP key]
name: gpucloud_hibernate_server
title: Hibernate a server
